question:
A 50-year-old male presents to his physician with a one-week history of intermittent lower back pain
that began after lifting heavy boxes at his workplace. He denies fever, chills, or weight loss. His medical
history is significant for recurrent peptic ulcer disease. He has no history of smoking or alcohol use.
Physical examination reveals normal vital signs and mild lumbar paraspinal tenderness, with no
neurological deficits. Spinal x-rays show no abnormalities. Which medication would be most
appropriate to prescribe? Answer Choices: (A) Amitriptyline (B) Tramadol (C) Naproxen (D) Prednisone
(E) Baclofen (F) Aspirin (G) Cyclobenzaprine (H) Acetaminophen (I) Ibuprofen (J) Diclofenac
 A. Tramadol
B. Cyclobenzaprine
C. Naproxen
D. Aspirin

E. Acetaminophen
F. Amitriptyline
G. Diclofenac
H. Ibuprofen
I. Baclofen
J. Prednisone
